_hinweis: Sentence patterns and target devices, English sample.
This file is copied to config/plugins/sprachsteuerung/saetze.json during
installation when the LoxBerry interface language is English, and is then
maintained by the user - a plugin update NEVER overwrites it.
Placeholders in curly braces:
{ziel}   resolved against the 'ziele' list including its aliases.
MAY BE ABSENT: if the sentence names no target, the room
configured on the microphone applies ('turn on' in the living
room).
{wert}   takes a number - as digits OR as a word ('fifty',
'one hundred and twenty', '21.5', 'twenty one point five').
{dauer}  takes a time span ('10 minutes', 'an hour', 'half an hour',
'an hour and a half', '2 hours and 30 minutes') or a time of
day ('at 10 pm', 'at 7:30', 'tomorrow at 7'). The command is
then scheduled and executed later. Where {dauer} does NOT
follow 'in' or 'after', the phrase must bring its own
preposition ('in 5 minutes', 'at 10 pm').
{rest}   takes arbitrary text and is available in the answer.
Alternatives go in square brackets separated by a vertical bar:
'turn [the|] light {ziel} on'
Case, umlauts and punctuation are normalised for the comparison.
A name only matches as a whole word: 'tor' does not match in 'motor'.
WHAT IS NOT SWITCHED: if the sentence holds a time phrase, a negation
('not', 'don't') or a second command ('... and the kitchen on') that
no rule takes up, the system asks back instead of ignoring the rest.
RANGE: a target may carry "min" and "max". A value outside is
rejected; without them, percent values must lie between 0 and 100.
IN THE ANSWER TEXT every field of the result can be used:
{zielname} {wert} {einheit} {dauer_s} {rest} {istwert}
ORDER MATTERS: the FIRST matching rule wins. More specific patterns
belong at the top - the self-test on the Test tab checks this and
names any shadowed rule.
WHY 'down' IS NOT AN OFF WORD: 'turn the kitchen down' means dimming,
not switching off. The plugin cannot dim by one step, so 'down' is
left out of the rules rather than mapped to off.
WHY on/off HAVE A FIXED POSITION HERE: a pattern like
[turn|switch] [off|] {ziel} [off|]
looks convenient but is ambiguous - with both particles optional,
{ziel} swallows the word 'off' and the ON rule wins. Measured on
24.08.2026: 'switch off the kitchen' switched the kitchen ON.
ASKING FOR A STATE ({istwert}): a target may carry a field 'url_lesen'.
The plugin fetches that address and inserts the answer as {istwert}.
SENSITIVE TARGETS: a target with "bestaetigen": true is not switched at
once - the system asks back, and only a 'yes' triggers it.
